title: Kernel Orchestrator Regulator for Variable Token Flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current kernel selection relies on coarse-grained heuristics that are tuned for static sequence-length buckets and per-architecture defaults. In mixed workloads where requests frequently alternate between short prefill-heavy prompts and long decode sessions (e.g., chat with long context + generation), we observe suboptimal kernel usage: higher P50/P95 latency and increased GPU cost due to frequent kernel switches that are not amortized, and KV cache pressure from suboptimal prefill-decoding routing. This ticket proposes a Kernel Orchestrator Regulator (KOR) that sits between the request router and the kernel runtime to make per-request kernel decisions based on a compact runtime feature vector and a low-latency online autotuner.

Proposal: Build a lightweight orchestrator that implements three capabilities:
1) Request fingerprinting: capture a short, fixed-size feature vector per request composed of architecture (arch fingerprint), requested max_tokens, current sequence length distribution estimate, and presence of attention patterns (dense vs sparse attention signals inferred from token types and model metadata). The fingerprinting is O(1) and stored in request metadata for downstream routing.
2) Regulator policy: a hybrid rule+learning policy that maps fingerprints to a kernel plan (prefill kernel, decode kernel, batch size hint, KV caching policy). The rule portion codifies safety constraints (latency SLOs, memory ceilings) per-customer tier; the learning portion is an online bandit/autotuner that tries compact kernel variants and records short-term latency/cost outcomes.
3) Stateful autotune loop: a low-overhead prober that runs micro-benchmarks asynchronously (on ~1-2% of traffic or isolated warmup traffic) and updates a lightweight cache of best kernel plans per (arch, seqlen-profile-bucket). The cache includes fallback plans and a confidence score that decays over time.

Design details:
- Fingerprint dimensions: arch_id, seq_len_hint, max_tokens_hint, is_prefill (boolean), historical tail_latency_bucket, model_family. Each dimension is a string/enum; the composed key is hashed to a short index.
- Kernel plan fields (strings): prefill_kernel_id, decode_kernel_id, batch_hint (small int), kv_policy (none|prefix|persist), switch_cost_estimate_ms.
- Autotuner: epsilon-greedy bandit with exponential decay on epsilon; prefer safety (do not pick kernel that violates recent latency SLOs). Use per-customer and global aggregates to avoid regressions on high-impact customers.
- Probing strategy: microbench kernels executed inside a sandboxed microqueue with strict time budget and eviction policy to avoid affecting production throughput. Probing frequency configurable via runtime feature flag.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit kernel_plan_assigned events with fingerprint hash, plan id, and estimated switch cost.
- Track per-plan metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, failure rate, GPU occupancy, memory high-water mark.
- Add an incident alarm if a new plan increases p95 by >15% over baseline for a sustained window.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end integration tests covering policy fallback and prober sandboxing.
- Microbench: for synthetic mixed workloads (50/50 short-long), KOR reduces average token cost by >=8% and improves p95 latency by >=10% compared to baseline heuristic router.
- No customer-facing regressions during canary (tracked by rollback trigger rules).
- Observability: dashboards for plan churn, per-arch plan quality, and probe outcomes.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement fingerprint and static policy in shadow mode (no effect on runtime) for 1 week to collect signals.
2) Enable canary with 2% traffic on a non-critical region; run for 72 hours and validate metrics.
3) Gradually ramp to 25% then 100% with automatic guardrails; keep prober off by default during canary.
4) Enable prober after 2 weeks behind feature flag; start with low frequency (0.5% of traffic).

Risks and mitigations:
- Probe-induced noise: sandbox probes on separate GPU queue and cap throughput.
- Cold-start for new models/arch combos: fallback to conservative kernel plan and schedule targeted microbenching.
- State explosion: bucket seq_len profiles into coarse clusters and evict low-traffic keys.

Dependencies: needs microbenchmark harness (ENG-27105), runtime eviction hooks (ENG-47290), and updated telemetry pipeline for new events.

Open questions:
- Should we support multi-kernel decode pipelines (stage kernel A for first N tokens then switch to B) or restrict to single decode kernel? Proposal: MVP uses single decode kernel per request and exposes staged pipelines as a follow-up.
- Cost accounting: tie per-plan cost estimates to the billing/quotas system or keep internal only? Recommendation: internal first, expose after two cycles of stable signals.
